findings.message: The equivalence test checks that each tool gives the same reply through step.call as when its handler is called directly. Both sides run the moved handlers, so the test cannot catch a change in behaviour introduced by the move itself. The LLD's migration step 2 and its test fixtures call for 'golden replies captured from the in-process handlers before the move'. No such golden fixture is used. Also, several tools reach only an early error reply in this test: insrc_analyze with no repo resolves to 'no repo', and review start against empty stream maps fails with unknown-method. This meets the plan's t8 check as written, but it falls short of the LLD's proof of ac1 ('same envelope as before the move').
findings.expectationRef: LLD migrationSteps[1] 'Capture golden replies of each tool called in-process for the equivalence tests' / testStrategy integration fixture 'golden replies captured from the in-process handlers before the move' (ac1)

findings.message: StepCallContext, StepToolName and their accessors (runInStepContext, stepCwd, stepEnvRepo, stepClient) are in src/shared/step-context.ts. The LLD places StepCallContext 'in the daemon's step host', and its callSites do not list src/shared. The move looks necessary: under the import-graph rule (ac4), the MCP forwarder cannot import src/daemon/steps, and src/analyze/context/scope.ts must also read the context. Still, it departs from the approved data model and should be written down in the build record.
findings.expectationRef: LLD dataModelChanges 'StepCallContext (new, in the daemon's step host)'

findings.message: The module moved from src/mcp/server.ts into the daemon's step tree but still logs as getLogger('mcp:server'). Its sibling host.ts uses 'daemon:step-host', so lines from this daemon-side code will be filed under the MCP server's logger name. Rename it to something like 'daemon:step-analyze-oneshot'.

AnalyzeOneShotDeps still declares `samplingSupported` and logs it, but this Story retires MCP sampling (McpSamplingProvider and the sampler context are deleted). The field is now unused and suggests sampling still matters. Drop it.

The temporary-Lance setup is pasted in between the existing imports. It brings in a second copy of node:test's `after` and of the node:fs, node:os and node:path imports under aliases (afterAllLance, mkdtempSyncLance, rmSyncLance, tmpdirLance, joinLance), even though mkdtempSync, rmSync, tmpdir and join are already imported a few lines below. Other test files put their imports first and setup after, without duplicate aliased imports.
Removing the sampler paragraph from the resolveShaperKind doc comment left a stray ` * *` line in the JSDoc block.

In the module header, a paragraph about the step context sits between items 3 and 4 of the numbered 'Resolution order' list, so item 4 ('undefined') reads as part of that paragraph. Move the paragraph after the list.

No build record was given, so I can't confirm that any promised test passes. Every promised test that can be seen in the diff is present but unverified: step host, equivalence of the seven tools, cancellation, state-store miss, in-daemon client equivalence, no loopback, resolveRepoPath, scope directoryOf, client identity, context isolation, and the workflow-rpc import checks. This is an unverified pass-state, not missing tests. Every changed symbol's testsReaching is empty, but this is diff-mode grounding (diff:<file> entities, no graph edges). The new tests in step-host.test.ts, in-daemon-client.test.ts and step-context.test.ts call host.ts, daemon-client.ts, resolve-repo.ts, analyze-oneshot.ts, scope.ts and shared/step-context.ts directly. So I'm not reporting the empty edges as coverage gaps.

The 'step.call' registration and installStepDaemonClient(createInDaemonClient(rpcHandlers, streamHandlers)) in main() are not exercised by any test visible in the grounding. step-host.test.ts builds its own copy of this wiring ('as index.ts registers them'). workflow-rpc-imports.test.ts only checks the import statically. The daemon's real wiring is reached only if mcp-process-e2e.test.ts or the smoke checks start a real daemon, and their content can't be seen here.

Present but unverified. forward-step.test.ts is in the changed set, but its hunk text was not provided, so I can't confirm the promised cases for the named forwarder errors and for progress relay are in it, or that they pass.

findings.message: Duplication: by its own header this file is 'a copy of src/mcp/resolve-repo.ts'. The same precedence chain (explicit repo > the registered repo containing cwd > INSRC_REPO > undefined) and the global _setResolveForCwdForTests override now live in two places. A later fix to the order or to the empty-string handling has to be made twice, or the MCP docgen/approve tools and the moved step tools will resolve repos differently. Better: one resolver in src/shared that takes the cwd/env/lookup sources as parameters, with each side passing its own.

Unhandled error path: the insrc_analyze entry casts args unchecked (`args as AnalyzeOneShotArgs`), and runAnalyzeOneShot never checks `focus`. The other six handlers parse their own args. If a forwarder sends args without a string `focus`, `intent.focus.slice(0, 80)` in the log call throws a TypeError, and the caller sees a 'step-failed' frame saying "Cannot read properties of undefined" instead of a clear 'focus is required' error. Check `focus` (and `repo`/`target`/`scope` types) before building the run params.

Correctness/resource risk: the stream signal is passed only to the review and code-review runners. insrc_analyze, insrc_analyze_step, insrc_workflow_step, insrc_build_step and insrc_triage ignore it. Now that these run inside the long-lived daemon instead of the per-session MCP process, a forwarder that disconnects (session closed, MCP restarted) no longer ends the work. A one-shot analyze or a workflow synthesize keeps running in the daemon, making model calls and possibly writing artifacts, with nobody to receive the result. Before the move, killing the MCP process stopped it.

If a stream handler throws synchronously instead of returning a rejected promise, the throw escapes `handler(params, send, inner.signal)` inside the Promise executor. The promise rejects, but `finish` never runs: the wait timer stays armed and the abort listener stays attached to opts.signal until the timer fires. Wrapping the call as `Promise.resolve().then(() => handler(...))` sends every failure through failWith.
The timeout message rounds `opts.timeoutMs / 60_000`, so any limit under 30 s reports 'within 0 minutes'.

Taste: the moved module still logs as 'mcp:server', and its deps keep `samplingSupported`, which MCP sampling's retirement in this same change makes meaningless. Daemon-side runs will be logged under the MCP server's name.
Taste: removing the sampler paragraph left a stray ` * *` line in the resolveShaperKind doc comment.

Taste: the Lance isolation preamble imports mkdtempSync/rmSync/tmpdir/join a second time under aliases (`mkdtempSyncLance` etc.) right above the file's existing imports of the same functions, and adds a second `after` import from node:test.

Test-helper duplication: `untilAborted` and the code-review deps/subject fixture (CREATED, GROUNDING, crSubject/crDeps) are re-declared almost word for word from in-daemon-client.test.ts. A shared test helper would keep the two in step.
